# Lyrd complete agent documentation

Version channel: stable (`npm latest`)
Core package: `@lyrd/core@0.2.0`
CLI package: `@lyrd/cli@0.3.0`
Documentation: https://seunjin.github.io/lyrd/
Repository: https://github.com/seunjin/lyrd

## 1. Product boundary

Lyrd manages modal interaction. It does not provide Dialog, Sheet, Drawer, Toast, focus management,
portals, or CSS.

Lyrd owns:

- typed app scopes for Alert and Confirm
- imperative Promise-based calls
- Confirm pending, error, and retry behavior
- custom JSX session results and close reasons
- a shared LIFO modal stack
- topmost checks and close lifecycle

The application owns:

- Alert and Confirm display fields
- JSX, CSS, copy, buttons, and error presentation
- Base UI, Radix, shadcn, or custom primitive composition
- custom modal component state and result types
- Toast and all non-modal notification behavior

## 2. Install and generated structure

```bash
pnpm dlx @lyrd/cli init
pnpm dlx @lyrd/cli add overlay --verbose
```

The CLI installs `@lyrd/core` and `@base-ui/react`, then creates app-owned files similar to:

```text
src/overlays/
  scope.ts
  OverlayProvider.tsx
  index.ts
  alert/AlertSurface.tsx
  confirm/ConfirmSurface.tsx
```

CSS Modules or Tailwind CSS v4 is selected during initialization. Existing files and application
entry points are not overwritten. Mount the generated Provider once at the application root.

## 3. Define an app scope

```tsx
import { createOverlayScope } from '@lyrd/core'
import type { ReactNode } from 'react'

type AppAlertRequest = {
  title: ReactNode
  description?: ReactNode
  actionLabel?: ReactNode
}

type AppConfirmRequest = {
  title: ReactNode
  description?: ReactNode
  confirmLabel?: ReactNode
  cancelLabel?: ReactNode
  tone?: 'neutral' | 'danger'
  onCancel?: () => void
}

export const appOverlay = createOverlayScope<{
  alert: AppAlertRequest
  confirm: AppConfirmRequest
}>()

export const useOverlay = appOverlay.useOverlay
```

The display field names are application decisions. Core reserves these behavior fields:

- Alert: `onAction?: () => void`
- Confirm: `onConfirm?: () => void | Promise<void>`
- Confirm: `closeOnEscape?: boolean`, `closeOnOutsidePress?: boolean`

Do not redeclare reserved fields in app request types.

## 4. Provider and renderers

```tsx
import type { OverlayRenderers } from '@lyrd/core'

const renderers = {
  alert: AlertSurface,
  confirm: ConfirmSurface,
} satisfies OverlayRenderers<AppOverlayRequests>

export function OverlayProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <appOverlay.OverlayProvider renderers={renderers}>
      {children}
    </appOverlay.OverlayProvider>
  )
}
```

Import `useOverlay` from this generated app module, not from a global Core hook. React-external code
and isolated tests can use `appOverlay.createClient()` and pass that client to the Provider.

## 5. Alert

```tsx
await overlay.alert({
  title: 'Saved.',
  actionLabel: 'OK',
  onAction: () => trackNotice(),
})
```

Alert returns an awaitable `OverlayHandle<void>`. Its Renderer receives `action()`. Calling it runs the
calling-side `onAction` synchronously, resolves the handle, and starts closing. Alert has no managed
pending, error, or retry UI. It does not close through ESC or outside press.

Use `onAction` for an optional synchronous side effect. Use Confirm or custom JSX when an action must
be awaited or retried.

## 6. Confirm

```tsx
const confirmed = await overlay.confirm({
  title: 'Delete this project?',
  confirmLabel: 'Delete',
  cancelLabel: 'Cancel',
  tone: 'danger',
  onConfirm: () => deleteProject(),
  closeOnEscape: false,
})
```

Confirm returns an awaitable `OverlayHandle<boolean>`:

- successful confirm: `true`
- cancel, ESC, outside, programmatic close, or route change: `false`

The Renderer receives `confirm()`. It invokes the calling-side `onConfirm`. While a returned Promise is
pending, duplicate confirm, cancel, ESC, and outside attempts are blocked. Rejection leaves the Confirm
open with `actionStatus: 'error'` and `error`; invoking `confirm()` again retries the same callback.

`onConfirm` is not merely a post-confirm event. It is the sync or async operation whose pending and
failure lifecycle Core manages. `confirm()` is the Renderer-to-Core command. This direction difference is
why only the caller callback has the `on` prefix.

Core does not reserve `onCancel`. If the app needs an explicit cancel-button side effect, add that field
to the app request type and invoke it in the Renderer before `cancel()`. Do not invoke it for ESC,
outside, or programmatic close.

## 7. Custom JSX

Use `open()` for Dialog, Sheet, BottomSheet, Drawer, and fullscreen modal UI.

```tsx
type ProjectResult = { name: string }

function ProjectEditor({ projectId }: { projectId: string }) {
  const session = useOverlaySession<ProjectResult>()
  const [name, setName] = useState('')

  return (
    <Dialog.Root
      open={session.open}
      onOpenChange={(open, details) => {
        if (!open) {
          session.requestClose(
            details.reason === 'escape-key' ? 'escape' : 'outside',
          )
        }
      }}
      onOpenChangeComplete={(open) => {
        if (!open) session.completeClose()
      }}
    >
      <ProjectForm
        projectId={projectId}
        name={name}
        onNameChange={setName}
        onCancel={() => session.close('cancel')}
        onSave={() => session.resolve({ name })}
      />
    </Dialog.Root>
  )
}

const outcome = await overlay.open<ProjectResult>(
  <ProjectEditor projectId={projectId} />,
  { closeOnEscape: true, closeOnOutsidePress: false },
)
```

The element and its props are a call-time snapshot. Parent re-renders do not replace the open element.
Keep form, step, and loading state inside the component. If it needs current external data, pass a
stable ID and subscribe to a store or query.

`open()` always creates a new independent session. There is no identity lookup, deduplication, or input
update API.

## 8. Outcome and handle

```ts
type OverlayOutcome<Result> =
  | { status: 'resolved'; value: Result }
  | { status: 'closed'; reason: OverlayCloseReason }

type OverlayCloseReason =
  | 'cancel'
  | 'escape'
  | 'outside'
  | 'route-change'
  | 'programmatic'
```

The return value of `open()` is a real Promise extended with `close()`:

```tsx
const editor = overlay.open<ProjectResult>(<ProjectEditor projectId={projectId} />)
editor.close('programmatic')
const outcome = await editor
```

Close targets:

- `overlay.close()`: topmost session owned by the client
- `handle.close()`: the exact session represented by the handle
- `overlay.closeAll()`: every session owned by the client

## 9. LIFO stack and lifecycle

New sessions are pushed on top. The most recently opened session receives ESC and topmost close first.
Opening a nested Confirm does not unmount the custom overlay below it, so local state is preserved.

Custom session contract:

```ts
type OverlayPhase = 'opening' | 'open' | 'closing'

type OverlaySession<Result> = {
  open: boolean
  phase: OverlayPhase
  resolve(value: Result): boolean
  close(reason?: OverlayCloseReason): boolean
  requestClose(reason: 'escape' | 'outside'): boolean
  completeClose(): void
}
```

- `resolve(value)`: settle with a resolved outcome and start closing.
- `close(reason)`: settle with a closed outcome and start closing.
- `requestClose(reason)`: ask Core to apply topmost and close-option checks.
- `completeClose()`: notify Core that exit animation ended and remove the session.

Keep closing sessions mounted until `completeClose()`. This also prevents repeated ESC from leaking to
the session below. The UI primitive and app CSS own nested focus, inert behavior, portals, and z-index.

Core does not install global keyboard or pointer listeners. Base UI, Radix, shadcn, or a custom modal
detects Escape and outside press; the app Renderer translates those events to `requestClose()`. When no
primitive is used, the app must also implement focus trapping and restoration, scroll locking, portal
behavior, and ARIA semantics. A modal without an exit animation may call `completeClose()` as soon as
the session enters `closing`.

## 10. Public application methods

```ts
overlay.alert(request)
overlay.confirm(request)
overlay.open<Result>(element, options?)
overlay.close(reason?)
overlay.closeAll(reason?)
```

Use only these documented application methods. Toast belongs to a separate app notification system.

## 11. Troubleshooting

Start with the first Lyrd error in the browser console, then distinguish these common failures:

- Every `useOverlay()` call fails: mount the generated `OverlayProvider` once above the application.
- Only one subtree fails: that component is outside the Provider's React tree, or imports `useOverlay`
  from a different app scope.
- The Provider rejects an injected client: create the Provider, Hook, and client from the same
  `createOverlayScope()` result.
- `useOverlaySession()` reports an invalid location: call it only inside a component passed to
  `overlay.open()`.
- The Promise settles but modal DOM or scroll lock remains: call `completeClose()` when the UI
  primitive finishes its exit transition.
- An already-open component does not receive changed parent props: props are a call-time snapshot;
  own changing state inside the component or subscribe by a stable ID.
- Next.js reports Hook, context, or event-handler errors: keep the root layout server-rendered, but
  put the generated Provider and every `useOverlay()` caller behind a `'use client'` boundary.

Complete recovery guide: https://seunjin.github.io/lyrd/troubleshooting
